javascript.subDescription: Master JavaScript from fundamentals to advanced AI integration. Build dynamic web apps and client-side LLM orchestrations.

phases.title: The Magic Behind the Screen: Logic & Basics
theory: The Big Three: Skeleton (HTML), Skin (CSS), and the Muscle (JS)
The Live Translator: How your browser reads code
Understanding the role of AI coding assistants (Cursor/Copilot) in JS generation
practicals: Secret Messages: Write your first `console.log`
Use an AI assistant to explain a piece of confusing JS syntax

phases.title: Data & Typing
theory: Liquid Containers: What 'Dynamic Typing' means
Primitives (Numbers, Strings, Booleans) and Non-Primitives (Objects, Arrays)
Handling JSON outputs from LLMs
practicals: The `typeof` Lab: Use the browser to reveal what data shapes are
Parse a mock AI JSON response into a JavaScript object

phases.title: Decision Making & Control Flow
theory: Conditional Logic: The 'If/Then' mindset
Comparison and Logical Operators (>, <, ===, &&, ||)
Ternary Operators for concise UI state toggles
practicals: The Gatekeeper: Check if a user's prompt is too long before sending to an API
The Grade Calculator logic flow

phases.title: Loops & Iteration
theory: The 'While' Loop and 'For' Loop
Iterating through Collections: Looking into arrays
Processing streamed tokens from an AI response loop
practicals: The List Reader: Print out every item in an AI-generated array
Create a 'typing effect' by looping over a string of text

phases.title: Functions & Arrow Syntax
theory: Input vs. Output: Arguments and Return
Reusable Logic vs Copy-Pasting AI generated code blindly
Arrow Functions: The Fast Shortcut and 'One-Liners'
practicals: The Greeting Machine: A function that takes a name and says 'Hello'
Rewrite 5 standard functions into modern Arrow Functions

phases.title: Modern Arrays & Strings
theory: The Modern Array: `map()`, `filter()`, and `reduce()`
Searching the Crowd: `find()`, `includes()`
Template Literals: Dynamic text injection for Prompt Engineering
practicals: Filter an array of user messages to find only flagged content
Build a dynamic AI prompt using Template Literals and variables

phases.title: Mastering Objects & Destructuring
theory: Objects as Profiles: Storing related data together
Destructuring: Taking only what you need from a big box
The Spread Operator (`...`): Merging states and configs
practicals: Extract `text` and `finishReason` from a massive LLM API response object
Merge a default AI configuration object with user-provided settings using `...`

phases.title: DOM Basics & Events
theory: The DOM: The browser's map of your HTML
Selectors: Finding elements by ID, Class, or Tag
Event Listeners: Handling button presses and keystrokes
Building Chat UIs: Capturing 'Enter' key to send messages
practicals: Create a dynamic list that appends new <li> elements for user messages
Capture a user's prompt via an input field and display it on the screen

phases.title: Async, Promises & Fetch APIs
theory: Synchronous vs. Asynchronous execution
Promises: Pending, Kept (Resolved), and Broken (Rejected)
Async/Await: The modern way to handle promises
Fetch API: Connecting to OpenAI or your backend API
practicals: Fetch a list of random facts from a public API
Build an async function that sends a prompt to a mock LLM and awaits the response

phases.title: Streaming AI Responses in the Browser
theory: Fetch Streams (`Response.body.getReader()`)
TextDecoder: Converting byte streams into readable text
Updating the DOM incrementally to create a typing effect
Handling API rate limits and timeouts
practicals: Consume a Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream using Fetch
Build a realtime AI typing UI that updates as chunks arrive

phases.title: Classes & Object Oriented JS
theory: Classes: The factory for creating objects
The Constructor: Setting up initial states
Extends & Super: Inheritance
Building a reusable `ChatClient` class
practicals: Build an `AiAgent` class with methods like `think()` and `act()`
Extend it into a `CodeAssistant` class with specialized system prompts

phases.title: The Event Loop & Call Stack
theory: The Single Thread: Why JS can only do one thing at a time
The Call Stack, Task Queue, and Microtasks
Why Promises execute before `setTimeout`
Keeping the UI responsive during heavy processing
practicals: Predict the order of logs between a `setTimeout` and a `Promise.resolve()`
Use `requestAnimationFrame` to maintain smooth UI animations

phases.title: Closures, Memory & Proxies
theory: Closures: Functions that carry surrounding variables
Garbage Collection and Memory Leaks (Watch out for zombie streams)
Proxies & Reflect: Intercepting object operations
Building reactive state systems from scratch
practicals: Create a closure that securely stores an API key and only returns the last 4 digits
Build a Proxy that logs an alert every time AI state data changes

phases.title: Client-Side AI (WebLLM & ONNX)
theory: Running LLMs entirely in the browser using WebGPU
WebLLM: Loading small models locally for zero-latency, private AI
ONNX Runtime Web: Running computer vision and NLP models on the client
Managing large asset downloads in the browser cache
practicals: Initialize a WebLLM engine in a service worker
Build an entirely offline chatbot using an in-browser model

phases.title: Fundamentals & Async
theory: Explain the difference between `let`, `const`, and `var`.
How does the Event Loop handle Promises vs `setTimeout`?
What is a Closure?
practicals: Write a fetch request using `async/await` and handle errors gracefully.

phases.title: Advanced Browser Architecture
theory: How would you consume a readable stream from a Fetch request?
Explain how memory leaks occur in modern SPAs and how to find them.
What are the benefits of running models via WebGPU (WebLLM) vs Server APIs?
practicals: Design a robust, memory-safe system for managing 100+ concurrent WebSockets or Streams.
